Unlike standard early ray termination which discovers occlusion after data is in the working set, this method incorporates visibility feedback into the loader to prevent loading or refining occluded areas beforehand [S1].

The claim states that standard early ray termination discovers occlusion after data is in the working set, whereas the described method incorporates visibility feedback into the loader to prevent loading/refining occluded areas beforehand. The evidence explicitly supports this in multiple places: 1) The 'Source [S1] notes' section contains a bullet point stating: 'Standard early ray termination discovers occluded areas only at rasterization time, after data is already in the working set. This method incorporates visibility information into the loader to prevent loading/refining occluded areas beforehand.' 2) The 'Source [S1] passages' section reiterates this in Section 4: 'Occlusion culling during ray accumulation is performed by early ray termination. This approach optimizes computations but is not optimal in terms of data management, since occluded areas are discovered only at rasterization time, after the data is already part of the working set. In order to avoid wasting GPU memory resources and exploit bandwidth, we have incorporated a feedback mechanism in the system, that allows us to exploit visibility information gathered during rendering in the loader.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
